title: Ecosystem Study
subtitle: Learning what companies need from site selection through operations.
html:
Open Ecosystem Network ↗

Project overview

During a conversation, Steve Hsu, Executive Director of the Arizona Trade & Investment Office in Taiwan, shared how he looks at Arizona’s industrial ecosystem. It prompted me to pay attention to what companies need from site selection through construction and operations, including land, utilities, regulation, taxation, suppliers, and professional services. I am grateful for his practical insights. They gave me a starting point for Arizona Chip Journey and Arizona Innovation Map, two personal projects I built using public information.

Framework source: Executive Director, Arizona Trade & Investment Office - Taiwan Steve Hsu (徐竹先) ↗

What I learned

I used to notice the site and investment amount first. Now I also ask what each stage requires: land, utilities, and transport when choosing a site; engineering and equipment support during construction; and materials, maintenance, and logistics once production begins.

For Arizona Chip Journey, I brought those questions to wafer surface preparation and looked at how chemicals and ultrapure water are supplied and what facilities the equipment needs. For Arizona Innovation Map, I practiced distinguishing factories, offices, and service locations and recording the public sources I found.

The most useful thing I gained was a better sense of where to start when I do not know something. When I see a site on the map, I ask what it does locally and how much I can confirm from public information. These are questions I can keep using as I learn.
